chain.line: A dense product keeps more data in view when space is compact.
Compact density sets a small spacing base.
The tight type scale is a plain recipe pick. No pack rule links it to the spacing base.

name: Dense data

picks.question: product-type
picks.rationale: People scan lots of data on one screen.

picks.question: users-and-context
picks.rationale: Most people arrive without an account and without training.

picks.question: accessibility-target
picks.rationale: AA is the commitment for this public site. AAA is a later choice.

picks.question: platforms
picks.rationale: The first surface is the website.

picks.question: team
picks.rationale: One person maintains this starter, so the list stays short.

picks.question: brand-variance
picks.rationale: This starter is one brand. A second brand is out of this recipe.

picks.question: density
picks.rationale: A dense product needs compact space so more data stays in view.

picks.question: voice
picks.rationale: The words should sound human and direct, not cute.

picks.question: contrast-metric
picks.rationale: The accessibility target names WCAG 2.2, so the metric should match it.

picks.question: scale-direction
picks.rationale: The step names should run from 50 light toward 1000 dark.

picks.question: css-unit
picks.rationale: Type and space should follow the reader's font size.

picks.question: structure-theme-separation
picks.rationale: A theme change must not require edits inside the components.

picks.question: color-space
picks.rationale: The ramp scheme is described in OKLCH so lightness can stay even.

picks.question: step-distance
picks.rationale: Equal lightness steps are easier to explain than deltaE2000.

picks.question: step-count
picks.rationale: Eleven names match the 50 to 950 set people already expect.

picks.question: lightness-curve
picks.rationale: Most interface color sits in the middle of the ramp.

picks.question: chroma-hue-shift
picks.rationale: The provisional brand is warm, so darker steps may shift warmer.

picks.question: seed-input
picks.rationale: One provisional hex is enough to name the terracotta seed.

picks.question: on-color-pairing
picks.rationale: Text and its surface should use one pair: surface and on-surface.

picks.question: contrast-check
picks.rationale: Contrast is a review step. This dictionary does not measure it.

picks.question: font-family
picks.rationale: A system sans font is enough until a custom font is chosen.

picks.question: type-scale-ratio
picks.rationale: The tight type scale is a recipe pick. No pack rule links it to spacing.

picks.question: base-font-size
picks.rationale: Dense labels use a 14 pixel body.

picks.question: line-height
picks.rationale: Short labels use a 1.3 line height.

picks.question: spacing-base
picks.rationale: Compact screens stay aligned on a 4-point base.

picks.question: spacing-scale
picks.rationale: Even space steps are easier to remember in a small system.

picks.question: radius-base
picks.rationale: Corners stay slight. Density does not set the radius.

picks.question: radius-progression
picks.rationale: Radius steps add a fixed amount. This is a recipe pick.

picks.question: theme-shape
picks.rationale: Light and dark are modifiers on one theme, not two products.

picks.question: shareable-item
picks.rationale: A team should get tokens, CSS, and components together.

picks.question: locked-at-init
picks.rationale: Tiers, the on-color pair, and CSS variable names stay fixed after init.

picks.question: token-tiers
picks.rationale: The starter keeps primitive, semantic, and component tiers.

picks.question: default-theme
picks.rationale: The page opens on the light set. Dark is a modifier.

serves: Lots of data on one screen.
summary: Compact density, a 4-point spacing base, and a tight type scale.
